name: Hyaluron pen (needle-free)
lead: The hyaluron pen is a handheld, needle-free device that uses compressed air or a spring mechanism to push hyaluronic acid filler through the skin surface. People use it to get fuller, more defined lips and to soften fine lines and folds such as nasolabial lines, aiming for a plumper, smoother look without a syringe, a clinic visit or the sting of needle injections.[1]

It has been promoted online for at-home use, and its appeal in surveys centres on accessibility, low cost and the absence of needles. A population-based survey of users and injectors found 53.4% used it for fuller lips.[1][2]

The US Food and Drug Administration issued a safety communication in October 2021 stating that needle-free devices have not been approved or evaluated for injecting dermal fillers, lack control over where filler is placed, and have been associated with serious injuries.[1] The same survey reported complications in about 79% of respondents.[1][2] A 2022 paper in Dermatologic Surgery described DIY hyaluron pen content on social media as a safety threat to viewers.[3]
infobox: Not approved for dermal filler injection (US)
Hyaluronic pen, Hyla-Pen, no-needle filler pen

paras: The device has a pumped or spring-loaded pressure chamber, a trigger and a single-use ampule of filler with a tiny opening; pressure drives a narrow jet into the skin without a needle.[1] The principle is adapted from medical jet injectors developed in the 1950s for vaccines and insulin.[1]

The most common use is lip augmentation, adding volume, shape and plumpness. The device is also marketed for fine lines and wrinkles around the nasolabial folds, marionette lines and forehead, and some promotional material describes facial contouring and nose reshaping.[1] Surveyed users cited accessibility as a reason for choosing it over a clinic.[2]

Popularity reportedly rose during the COVID-19 pandemic through TikTok and Instagram tutorials, with tens of millions of views on related hashtags.[1] Names in use include hyaluronic pen, Hyla-Pen and no-needle filler pen.[1]
Names and marketing terms vary by market; in Spanish-speaking regions, particularly Mexico, it is often called a pluma hialurónica.[1]

Reported adverse events include infection, bleeding, bruising, swelling, asymmetry, scarring, discolouration, lumps, vascular occlusion with tissue necrosis, and permanent damage.[1][3] Dermatology and plastic surgery authorities cite imprecise depth and volume control and non-medical-grade or non-sterile filler as contributors.[1] The device is not authorised for this use in the US or Canada, while in Mexico it is described as largely unregulated.[1]
Online, it is presented as a cheap, painless way to get fuller lips at home. A survey found 53.4% of users sought fuller lips and cited accessibility as a reason for use.[1]

No controlled trials of the device have been found. Observational work includes a 2024 survey of users and injectors reporting that most had complications, many requiring hyaluronidase, surgery or emergency care.[1][2] A 2022 analysis examined social media posts about the device.[3]

card.summary: A high-pressure needle-free filler injector sold for DIY lips; the FDA warns against it and surveys report frequent complications.
card.aka: Hyaluronic pen, Hyla-Pen, no-needle filler pen
card.note: FDA safety communication (2021): not approved for filler injection; serious injuries reported.

quick.overview:
The hyaluron pen shoots hyaluronic acid filler into the skin with pressure instead of a needle. It is marketed online for fuller lips and wrinkles.

The FDA has warned that such devices are not approved for this use.
quick.mechanism: Compressed air or a spring forces a thin jet of filler through the skin surface, with depth and volume depending on pressure and technique.
quick.risks: Reported problems include infection, lumps, scarring, vascular occlusion with tissue death and permanent damage. A survey found about 79% of users reported complications.

chain: Pressure jet drives hyaluronic acid gel into the lip or skin
Filler adds volume under the surface
Fuller lips and softened lines, as users describe
angle.text: Users and sellers present the pen as a painless way to plump lips and smooth lines at home. Dermatology bodies and the FDA have said the devices have not been evaluated for this purpose and cannot control filler placement.
